subject: AscendAI — post-call econ synthesis & prioritized next steps
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Nair <rajesh@ascendai.com>, Elena Soto <elena@ascendai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: AscendAI — post-call econ synthesis & prioritized next steps

Hi Rajesh / Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the priority asks so we can move the pilot forward. I wrote this to lock in what we heard and to surface a couple of low-friction next steps.

TL;DR (ask): Confirm approval to proceed with a 6-week pilot scoped to 3 use-cases (chat support, document summarization, fraud triage) and confirm budget owner + procurement timeline. We attached a draft SOW and a short econ workbook.

What you told us (pain points)
- Token spend volatility: large spikes during end-of-month reporting windows that blow out compute spend.
- Tail latency at peak traffic affects agent-to-customer handoffs (p99 spikes ~700-900ms).
- Need to meet data residency / audit log requirements for regulated customers.
- Tight pilot budget with procurement gate set at ~$40k/month run-rate for any sustained service.

Goals we’ll measure in pilot
- Reduce per-token compute spend (equivalent) by 30–45% while keeping p95 within 150ms for chat flows.
- Maintain semantic fidelity: <5% regression on our eval prompts for summarization.
- Validate rollback/fallback behavior and audit logs for compliance flows.

Initial economic model (high level) — please confirm your current baseline numbers if you have them: 
- Estimated current usage: 36.5M tokens / month across the three use-cases.
- Our baseline compute-cost proxy used on call: $0.0015 / token -> monthly ~ $54,750.
- Pilot target: 35–40% reduction via batching (continuous windows + smart concat), KV/prefix caching for repeated context, and model quantization where acceptable.
- Example outcome (conservative): 35% reduction -> ~$19k/month savings (new monthly ~ $35.6k). Upside scenario (45%): ~ $24.6k savings.

Operational levers we propose for the pilot
- Continuous batching with dynamic time-based flush (20–40ms window) for stateless routes.
- Per-route KV caching for repetitive prompts (support templates & escalations).
- One quantized candidate for low-risk summarization pipelines (A/B traffic to monitor quality).

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Confirm budget guardrail (is $40k/month the procurement threshold?) and who owns the purchase (procurement / IT contact).
2) Approve the attached SOW draft and econ workbook so we can finalize dates (we suggested Nov 29 start).
3) Share any existing p95/p99 traces for the three use-cases so we can tune batching windows in week 0.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-econ.xlsx (workbook, small modeling tabs); SOW-draft.pdf (pilot scope + roles + timeline).

If that aligns, I’ll loop Marissa for SOW signature and Ben will run a short latency-sensitivity plan with your engineers next week.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Mateo Alvarez

If you can answer 1–2 in short form we’ll try to make a yes/no decision on the SOW by end of week.

Rajesh — quick technical note on the batching/latency trade-off and the sensitivity numbers Mateo put forward.

- Batching & tail latency: continuous batching with a short time-based flush (we usually start at 20ms for high-traffic interactive routes) reduces compute per-token and amortizes kernel launch cost. For 20–40ms windows we typically see an increase in median latency of ~10–25ms but can push p99 up depending on request size/sequence length. The key is per-route SLOs: keep chat routes at a tighter flush (20ms + adaptive burst bypass) and use larger windows only for background summarization. In our experience, this keeps p95 essentially flat and limits p99 regressions to ~50–120ms in the worst-case peak.

- Cost sensitivity (modeling basis): Mateo used a blended compute proxy of $0.0015/token (this was a quick on-call proxy — we can refine). Below are example monthly compute-cost proxies by token volume at the $0.0015 baseline (before any levers):
  • 20M tokens -> $30,000
  • 36.5M tokens -> $54,750
  • 50M tokens -> $75,000

If we apply the pilot levers and assume the conservative 35% reduction, your monthly compute-cost would fall to: 20M -> $19.5k; 36.5M -> $35.6k; 50M -> $48.8k.

- Quick ops plan for pilot week 0: we’ll ingest sample traces, run a 2-day synthetic load to test batching windows and measure p95/p99, and then lock traffic routing rules. That test lets us pick a starting flush window that minimizes p99 impact on chat.

I can put together a short sensitivity tab in the attached workbook showing those three volume points plus a slider for % savings — will send an updated file by EOD.

• Budget: we can approve up to $40k/month sustained; for anything above that we’ll need a 2-sided credit or engineering sponsorship for the first 6 weeks.
• Data & traces: I’ll share a span export and the p95/p99 traces for chat and summarization by EOD tomorrow.

Marissa — could you please send the SOW-draft.pdf to our procurement team (procurement@ascendai.com) and include a short note on pilot cancellation terms? Also, if you can add a simple clause about audit log delivery cadence, that would speed legal review.

If we get the SOW routed this week we should be able to sign and stand up the pilot by early December.

Cheers —
Rajesh
